subject: POC visibility & acceptance checklist — Acme Cloud trial
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC visibility & acceptance checklist — Acme Cloud trial

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have a single plan for the 4-week POC you requested.

Recap (from discovery)
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for low-latency customer-facing recommendations at Acme’s catalog scale (~100 concurrent sessions, 2k tokens/session).
- Critical non-functional: 95th percentile latency <= 150ms for generate calls; end-to-end traceability for every customer request; audit log export to your Splunk instance.

Proposed POC scope & success criteria (draft) — see attached poc_acceptance_criteria.xlsx for details:
1) Performance: 95th pctl end-to-end latency <= 150ms under a 100-concurrent session synthetic workload (pass/fail).
2) Quality: Top-3 reranked suggestions contain at least one business-relevant item in 80% of sampled prompts (we will co-design a 100 prompt eval set).
3) Observability: Traces for each request exported to your Zipkin-compatible collector AND logs shipped to Splunk; dashboard with error rate, p95 latency, token cost per request.
4) Security/ops: Key rotation proof-of-concept + audit logs for inference requests.

Timeline
- Week 0 (this week): Confirm success criteria/owners, provide access to a small sample catalog and eval prompts.
- Week 1: Deploy trial model, set up routing, and enable telemetry exports.
- Week 2: Run synthetic load and initial evals; iterate.
- Week 3: Joint validation, capture dashboards for acceptance.

Owners (suggested)
- Redwood infra + observability: Karthik Iyer (will provision endpoints + trace/log export).
- Redwood CS / evals: Marissa Cole (will coordinate prompt set and quality scoring).
- Acme infra/plat: Emily Park / platform@acmecloud.com (provide Splunk endpoint & sample dataset).

Immediate asks for acme:
- Provide Splunk ingest endpoint + test token (or let us ship to a shared liveness bucket).
- Share 100-sample prompts (even anonymized) by EOD Thu.

If that looks right I’ll: (a) lock the success criteria spreadsheet and (b) schedule a 30-min kickoff tomorrow to confirm access and owners.

Thanks —
Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: poc_acceptance_criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), redwood-observability-checklist.md (text stub)

Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear summary. A few notes from our side: 

- Splunk: we'll provide an HEC token and endpoint (will share with Karthik).

- Latency: 150ms p95 is aggressive but we want to see the end-to-end number. If needed we can accept 250ms as fallback for first pass, with a target to optimize.
- Security: we'll need proof of audit log export and a basic key-rotation demo during week 2.

Happy to do the kickoff tomorrow 11:00–11:30 PT. Confirm and I’ll block.

Best,
Emily

All — quick status update on infra/observability tasks.

- Endpoints: spun up trial endpoint group in us-west-2 (ephemeral) and provisioned api keys for the trial; sending secure share to Emily.
- Tracing/logs: enabled OpenTelemetry tracing on the trial runtime; configured a Zipkin-compatible collector and tested trace export (sample traces attached).
- Splunk: I configured a receiving proxy and validated HEC ingestion with a test event from our staging account. Need Emily's real HEC token to finish end-to-end.
- Dashboards: created a baseline Grafana board tracking: request rate, errors (5xx), p50/p95 latency, avg token cost per request, cache hit rate. Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/AcmeTrial/generic-dashboard-ACME

Blocking items:
- Real dataset for realistic perf runs (Emily — ETA on the 100 prompts?).
- Splunk HEC token for final log export.

ETA for full trial readiness: Wed EOD (pending dataset + HEC token).

Thanks,
Karthik
